refuter_findings.evidence: The page says “At the regular point, the transfer matrix is the oriented cyclic shift.” But [[lem-qsmx-transfer-regular-point]] states “t(0)=i^N U”; for N=3 this is t(0)=-iU, not U. The summary omits a scalar that changes the asserted equality.

The title says “Regular Bethe data diagonalize the transfer family,” which asserts a common eigenbasis. The Statement establishes an eigenpair for each specified nonzero regular datum and expressly makes “no ... completeness” claim, so it does not establish diagonalization of the family.

The item lists [[thm-qsmx-transfer-commutativity]] as a mathematical prerequisite, but its Definition uses the monodromy definition to construct the shifted operators, then defines regular data by root conditions and a nonzero vector. It makes no commutativity claim and does not use the commutativity theorem; this is an unnecessary logical dependency edge.

The item’s locator says “Section 4 ... equations (113)–(115).” In the cited [Faddeev PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/9605187), section 5 begins before equation (113), under the heading “XXX1/2 model. Physical spectrum in the ferromagnetic thermodynamic limit”; equations (113)–(115) therefore are not in section 4. The item's local proof still establishes its eigenvalue.

reader_findings.evidence: The summary says “the transfer matrix is the oriented cyclic shift,” but lem-qsmx-transfer-regular-point establishes t(0) = i^N U. For N=3 the factor is -i, so the summary should state the factor or say “proportional to” the shift.

“Regular Bethe data diagonalize the transfer family” may imply completeness. The theorem proves eigenpairs for the stated regular data and explicitly makes no completeness claim. This is a suspected title overstatement; the proof itself is sound.

The item declares thm-qsmx-transfer-commutativity as a mathematical prerequisite, but its definition of the shifted monodromy, root conditions, and nonzero Bethe vector uses only def-qsmx-rational-monodromy. The commutativity theorem is not invoked. Unless it supplies an unstated meaning of “on-shell,” this is an unnecessary logical dependency edge.

The locator identifies PDF pp. 15–16, equations (113)–(115), as the one-particle momentum and energy source. Faddeev gives the one-particle energy dispersion in equations (109)–(112), p. 15; equations (113)–(115), p. 16, concern logarithmic Bethe equations, large-N momenta, and the scattering matrix. The separate Lecture 10 citation supports the dispersion in its own normalization, and the item's local proof establishes its stated normalization.
